_doc: The sea slugs' species with no name yet (Pierre, 2026-11-17, Q389 (2); study docs/reviews/2026-11-17-seaslug-undescribed-species-study.md): each defined by a published source (rule C2) and found on iNaturalist through the observation field its identifiers keep, since iNaturalist holds no taxon for it. Hand-kept but for `presence`, which tools/fetch_seaslugs.py --informal measures. Read by tools/fetch_seaslugs.py (its candidates, key = the data/seaslug-cand.json key), tools/judging_fish.py --subject seaslug and tools/seaslug_game.py (a species sheet of its genus while the species are not units, #975). Never a guide's number (the 2018 guide is not a source here: Pierre, 2026-11-17).
rule: Present when the observations carrying the label in the Philippines (Research Grade or Needs ID) have at least 3 distinct observers (tools/presence.py label_confirmed; Pierre, 2026-11-17, Q389 (2)); near Dauin: 2 within the centre's radius (near_dauin). Its candidates: observations with the label, at the genus, the genus agreed by 2 current identifications (tools/fetch_seaslugs.py agreed).

species.name: Goniobranchus sp. 5
species.cite: Soong, G.Y., Wilson, N.G. & Reimer, J.D. (2020). A species complex within the red-reticulate Goniobranchus Pease, 1866 (Nudibranchia: Doridina: Chromodorididae). Marine Biodiversity 50: 25.
species.defined: One of the five species-level clades of the red-reticulate Goniobranchus that Soong et al. (2020) delimit with COI and 16S rDNA (ABGD; maximum likelihood and Bayesian trees); none of the clades' morphotypes matches the original descriptions of G. reticulatus or G. tinctorius (the abstract). Its live animals are in the paper's supplementary Fig. S3 (not read: subscription). Mehrotra et al. 2021 (ZooKeys 1042: 73-188) cite it from the Philippines, Indonesia, Japan and Australia.
